nodes.label: TableNoCell::heads_up_is_symmetric (asymmetry guard)
nodes.rationale: Delegate-on-asymmetry was chosen over eliminating showdown_headsup entirely to preserve the TableAction::PlayerWins event signature for symmetric heads-up, avoiding a downstream-visible event-log break.

nodes.label: Hand<const N: usize> unification proposal
nodes.rationale: Unifies Two..Seven under one const-generic type while keeping compile-time size guarantees and const hand constants; eliminates ~80% impl duplication. Deferred because it is a multi-week invasive refactor touching ~100 importing files; type aliases would mitigate call-site churn.

nodes.label: Compile-time 5-card permutation tables
nodes.rationale: Six and Seven hard-code their choose-5 permutation tables as const arrays so the compiler can unroll/vectorise the HandRanker loop; a Box<[Card]> deck would force runtime permutation generation and a fallible or generic trait.

nodes.label: Mental Poker (trustless dealing problem)
nodes.rationale: Separates the state-coordination problem (replicated state machine over a signed hash-linked log) from the card-secrecy problem (threshold encryption + verifiable shuffles). Known unsolved pain points: the drop-out problem, settlement being separate from dealing, and collusion being unfixable by crypto.

nodes.label: Kaleidoscope / ROYALE — poker with payment and penalty enforcement
nodes.author: David, Dowsley, Larangeira
nodes.rationale: Addresses the two gaps mental poker alone leaves open: real-money settlement and the dropout/penalty problem, via blockchain escrow and slashing.
nodes.norm_label: kaleidoscope / royale — poker with payment and penalty enforcement

nodes.label: VTMF (verifiable l-out-of-l threshold masking function)
nodes.rationale: Barnett-Smart's core abstraction: threshold ElGamal exposing keygen/mask/remask/unmask; staged unmasking implements reveal-to-one (hole cards) vs full unmask (board/showdown) via reveal tokens with Chaum-Pedersen proofs.

nodes.label: Signed hash-linked event log (replicated state machine)
nodes.rationale: State is the deterministic fold over a verifiable log; prev_hash chaining makes history tamper-evident, turn structure replaces consensus for ordering, and signatures stop impersonation. Equivocation is detectable but only prevented with a broadcast layer.
nodes.norm_label: signed hash-linked event log (replicated state machine)

nodes.label: CardCrypto trait (swappable mental-poker crypto seam)
nodes.rationale: Design seam: pkcore's engine only ever sees plaintext Cards and DealerActions; all crypto is verified at the node boundary. A PlaintextCrypto mock proves the integration before swapping in BayerGrothCrypto with zero engine changes.

nodes.label: Coordinator trait (transport/ordering seam)
nodes.rationale: The only thing that differs across the six deployment architectures (in-process, P2P mesh, relay, semi-trusted coordinator, state channel, fully on-chain): each becomes one Coordinator impl with publish/next_event/head.

nodes.label: pkcore-mp crate skeleton (mental poker layer for pkcore)
nodes.norm_label: pkcore-mp crate skeleton (mental poker layer for pkcore)

nodes.label: QR codes as state sync beacon / offline transport
nodes.rationale: QR fits sync pointers, per-turn deltas, and signed checkpoints (~under 1.5KB practical limit) but not the masked deck or shuffle proofs, which need animated fountain-coded QR (BC-UR style). A QR shown to the whole table is a physical broadcast that attacks equivocation.
nodes.norm_label: qr codes as state sync beacon / offline transport

nodes.label: GameRules trait (generic card-game engine abstraction)
nodes.rationale: Don't unify on a Game object — poker, Go Fish, and trick-taking share no honest shape there. Unify one level lower on a card-operations-over-zones algebra plus a zone/visibility model; view_for is the hidden-information projection and the seam the crypto layer plugs into.

nodes.label: tricktaking crate (trick-taking family layer for bridge/spades)
nodes.rationale: Family mid-layer owning trick state, follow-suit legality, and trump resolution (~70-80% of trick-taking games), exposing only trump/can_play/score hooks so bridge and spades stay thin; the auction is deliberately not modeled because bidding is where per-game volume lives.
nodes.norm_label: tricktaking crate (trick-taking family layer for bridge/spades)

nodes.label: Interior mutability pattern (Cell/RefCell &self mutation)
nodes.rationale: TableCelled wraps every mutable field in Cell/RefCell so all methods take &self, enabling shared-reference observers and free-function showdown, at the cost of runtime double-borrow panics, RefCell counter overhead on hot paths, and borrow-scope discipline by convention rather than compiler enforcement. Neither design is thread-safe (Cell/RefCell are !Sync). For the single-controller game loop, TableNoCell is the cleaner design.

nodes.label: Dual game-engine maintenance risk (TableCelled vs TableNoCell)
nodes.rationale: All three audits converge: two parallel large engines create double maintenance, semantic drift, and unclear downstream guidance. Recommendation is to designate TableNoCell the canonical engine (bot sim already uses it exclusively; &mut self suits gRPC/async) and freeze or deprecate the Cell-based engine.
nodes.norm_label: dual game-engine maintenance risk (tablecelled vs tablenocell)

nodes.label: Panic-capable static initializers (LazyLock + unwrap)
nodes.rationale: Static initializers doing file I/O and unwrap (BC_RANK_HASHMAP, NAMER) can fail at module load before callers can handle errors; recommended pattern is OnceLock<Result<...>> with a fallible loader and a PKError variant for diagnosability.

nodes.label: Panic-capable operator overloads on Cards (todo!() in BitAnd/BitOr/BitXor)
nodes.rationale: Operator call sites look like safe idiomatic Rust (hand & board), compile cleanly, pass Clippy, then panic at runtime; flagged as P0 because operators will be used without suspicion. todo!() as a technical-debt tracker is dangerous on fundamental operators of a widely-used public type.
nodes.norm_label: panic-capable operator overloads on cards (todo!() in bitand/bitor/bitxor)

nodes.label: Pile trait over-specification (root cause of todo!/unimplemented! proliferation)
nodes.rationale: Pile defines a broad contract including operations semantically inapplicable to fixed-size types (add() on a Five), systematically pressuring every new type toward unimplemented!(). Recommended split into CardContainer / GrowableCards / Evaluatable composable traits, or short-term documented contract with non-panicking defaults.
nodes.norm_label: pile trait over-specification (root cause of todo!/unimplemented! proliferation)

nodes.label: TDA Rule 41 (short all-in BB: call target stays at configured blind)
nodes.rationale: Standard cardroom rule: an all-in-for-less BB does not discount the call; chip conservation is preserved by pot stratification (main pot capped at the all-in, side pots above it, single-contestant excess returned uncalled). The 0.0.48 change conflated 'BB can only win the all-in amount' with 'callers commit only the all-in amount'.
nodes.norm_label: tda rule 41 (short all-in bb: call target stays at configured blind)

nodes.label: Pot stratification / uncalled-bet return invariant
nodes.rationale: A winner's award from a pot layer is bounded by their commitment to that layer; folded contributions are awarded by layer but folders cannot win; a layer with a single contributor is uncalled and returned. Audit heuristic: never conflate what-actually-happened fields with rule-derived fields.

nodes.label: Probabilistic raise gate (anti-escalation invariant)
nodes.rationale: A deterministic equity-based raise branch made two strong-handed bots raise each other into all-in every hand. The fix gates raises at probability aggr.max(0.5) so raise sequences decay geometrically. Trade-off: slightly less realistic (GTO bot calls ~50% with aces) in exchange for multi-bot simulation stability. Test pattern: stochastic branches need a seeded multi-trial test asserting both outcomes occur.

nodes.label: Three analysis perspectives: Booth, Player, Spectator
nodes.rationale: Booth view (god mode, all hands visible — coded first), Player view (single known hand, leads to GTO/range thinking and the AJo+ DSL), Spectator view (no hands visible, requires stacks/blinds/bet data). Domain-first development: lock down pure card-odds analysis before bets and stack sizes.
nodes.norm_label: three analysis perspectives: booth, player, spectator

nodes.label: Domain-driven design applied to cards (French deck = domain, game = business requirements)
nodes.rationale: The same 52-card French-deck domain supports completely different business logic (Hold'em, Razz, Bridge, Blackjack); small business-requirement changes like Deuces Wild explode business-logic complexity (52^n re-evaluations).
nodes.norm_label: domain-driven design applied to cards (french deck = domain, game = business requirements)

nodes.label: Cactus Kev evaluator (7462 distinct hand values, prime-number encoding)
nodes.norm_label: cactus kev evaluator (7462 distinct hand values, prime-number encoding)

nodes.label: Suit transposition (covered/smothered/scattered equivalence classes)
nodes.rationale: Preflop matchup odds depend only on ranks plus whether players share suits (covered = one shared suit, smothered = both, scattered = none), so one calculation can be transposed across suit variations instead of recomputing; simple one-step suit shifting covers only 4 of 6 variations because two-removed suit pairs have a single direct transposition.

nodes.label: Preflop Odds Web Cache Service
nodes.rationale: The 4GB Binary Card Map (BCM) file takes several minutes to lazy-load on first call, making CLI use nearly useless despite 8-second odds calculation; a containerized web service caching preflop results amortizes the load cost. Candidate architectures: Swagger/OpenAPI REST on Docker, or protocol-buffer backed.

nodes.label: Split Pots / Round Equity
nodes.rationale: Side pots are the 'final boss' of poker logic: a complex state machine isolated as a matrix of per-player round investment. The standard AI solution shape (Vec<Player>, chips) felt clunky; bit flags tracking players per investment level were preferred. Edge case driving the design: all players all-in where the richest player's excess above the next-richest must be returned and their state switched from AllIn to Bet.

nodes.label: Seatbit
nodes.rationale: A simple integer storing a 1 bit for each active Seat, used to track which players share a committed bet level (e.g. x_highest_bet returns (Seatbit, amount) with tied seats combined into one Seatbit).

nodes.label: Omaha Hi-Lo (8 or Better)
nodes.rationale: Pot split between best high and best qualifying low (five unpaired cards 8 or lower, ace plays low). High and low are ranked independently per hole-card combination, so all 60 permutations iterate twice. Pot-splitting belongs in the dealer/game layer, not hand ranking.

nodes.label: Razz Variant
nodes.rationale: Seven-Card Stud played for A-5 low with no qualifier. CaliforniaHandRank already enumerates all valid Razz hands; remaining work is a RazzHand struct doing the C(7,5)=21 minimum search. Suggested first variant to implement.

nodes.label: Limit Hold'em Variant
nodes.rationale: Hand ranking identical to NLHE; the difference is entirely betting structure (fixed small/big bets, 4-raise cap per street). Primarily a pkdealer concern; pkcore only needs the BettingStructure type.

nodes.label: Seven-Card Stud Variant
nodes.rationale: Hand ranking reuses the existing Seven C(7,5) machinery; the hard part is the street model (bring-in, per-player up-cards, action order by best visible hand) which doesn't fit the Hold'em-centric Board type.

nodes.label: Stud Hi-Lo (Eight or Better)
nodes.rationale: Largely composition once StudHand and RazzHand exist: rank high with StudHand, low with RazzHand, return (Eval, Option<LowEval>). Implement last — most complex, depends on everything above.

nodes.label: BettingStructure Enum (proposed)
nodes.rationale: Proposed enum NoLimit / PotLimit / FixedLimit { small_bet, big_bet } extending ForcedBets, needed for Limit Hold'em and useful for Pot-Limit Omaha.

nodes.label: Combo Blocking
nodes.rationale: Cards a player holds cannot be in the villain's range. Versus::remaining() does this for hero's two cards; the audit goal is that every equity computation path applies the removal consistently, especially range vs range.

nodes.label: Counterfactual Regret Minimization (CFR)
nodes.rationale: Regret = how much you regret not taking a different action; counterfactual = weighted by the probability of reaching the decision given the opponent's strategy; minimization via regret-matching. Key theorem: in two-player zero-sum games, if both players minimize regret independently, the average strategy across iterations converges to a Nash equilibrium — you play the running average, not the current iteration.

nodes.label: Exploitability Metric
nodes.rationale: Chips/100 hands a strategy loses to the best-response opponent; Nash equilibrium has exploitability 0, practical solvers target < 0.1 chips/100. True computation needs a separate best-response tree pass.

nodes.label: CFR+ Algorithm
nodes.rationale: Two changes over vanilla CFR: regret floor (clamp accumulated regret to max(0, value), discarding stale negative regret) and linear strategy weighting (iteration t weighted by t), down-weighting chaotic early iterations automatically.

nodes.label: Discounted CFR (DCFR)
nodes.rationale: Generalizes CFR+ with alpha-discounted regrets (factor t^a/(t^a+1)) and beta-discounted strategy sums. Recommended alpha=1.5, beta=0; converges 2-10x faster than vanilla CFR on typical poker spots with no extra per-iteration cost. Chosen as the default CfrVariant.

nodes.label: Kuhn Poker Game
nodes.rationale: Canonical minimal poker: 3-card deck (J/Q/K), two players, one ante, one betting round, 12 terminal nodes. Its Nash equilibrium is known analytically (parameterized by alpha in [0,1/3], game value -1/18 for Player 0), making it the standard benchmark for verifying CFR solver implementations before scaling to Hold'em trees.

nodes.label: rs-poker Library (external)
nodes.author: Elliott Clark
nodes.rationale: Elliott Clark's Rust poker library, studied deliberately only through its testing toolchain (not its source) as a 'Rust for Failures' exercise. It surfaced nextest, cargo-mutants, cargo-fuzz, cargo llvm-cov, and mise build management.

nodes.label: Mutation Testing (cargo-mutants)
nodes.rationale: cargo-mutants mutates source operators (e.g. replacing | with ^ in src/bard.rs) and reports MISSED mutants the test suite fails to catch — immediately found gaps in Bard's bitwise trait impls.

nodes.label: cargo-nextest Test Runner
nodes.rationale: Adopted to replace cargo test; per-test timing surfaced slow low-value tests (e.g. a 19s Kuhn CFR convergence test) which were flagged #[ignore] to speed up builds.

nodes.label: Solid Domain Kernel Principle
nodes.rationale: pkcore's imperative: a universal core poker library usable as the foundation for table mechanics, hand evaluation, solvers, GTO tools, networked AI/bot play, and cheat detection — runnable on servers, web, and mobile. Architectural thesis: domains should have a battle-tested, rock-solid kernel definition of truth, so everything above it can be broken at will.

nodes.label: pkdealer Repository (external)
nodes.rationale: Sibling repo owning the gRPC platform layer: pkdealer_service, spectator web app, OTel instrumentation, and bot agent binaries. pkcore owns the poker logic; pkdealer owns the networking.

nodes.label: Range Frequency Suffix Notation (:f)
nodes.rationale: Range strings like 'AA:0.5, KK, QQ:0.75' express mixed strategies — standard GTO solver notation. Frequency cannot live on Combo (a Copy type used as HashMap key; f64 lacks Hash/Eq), so it belongs in WeightedCombos, which already stores per-combo u8 frequency. Out-of-range frequencies return PKError::InvalidFrequency.

nodes.label: EPIC-26: Player Action Tracking & Opponent Insights
nodes.norm_label: epic-26: player action tracking & opponent insights

nodes.label: Exploitation-as-Wrapper Pattern
nodes.rationale: Rather than fork RuleBasedDecider into an exploitative twin, exploitation is a modifier: a decider wrapping any inner BotDecider that adjusts the BotProfile from opponent stats at decision time, then forwards. Composable (any decider gains exploitation for free), zero trait churn, unit-testable as a pure function; cost is one small BotProfile clone per decision.

nodes.label: EPIC-28 Sketch: Cross-Session Profile Training
nodes.rationale: Follow-on: tune ExploitConfig's ~20 bounded scalars (multipliers, thresholds, sample gates) against a static field of bot profiles via CMA-ES or regret-matching, scoring runs by chip delta / BB/100, persisting trained configs as YAML. Reuses SimTable::run_n_hands and the CFR/DCFR regret primitives.

nodes.label: EPIC-DEFECT: Min-raise rule not enforced by TableCelled
nodes.norm_label: epic-defect: min-raise rule not enforced by tablecelled

nodes.label: Feature: Activate Unused Bluff & Check-Raise Fields
nodes.norm_label: feature: activate unused bluff & check-raise fields

nodes.label: CMA-ES Optimisation
nodes.rationale: Chosen over regret-matching (designed for discrete normal-form games) and simple (1+lambda)-ES (slower convergence, no covariance structure) because the problem is ~16-dimensional continuous optimisation with noisy fitness and no analytic gradient; the cmaes crate is actively maintained.

nodes.label: Paired-Seed Variance Reduction
nodes.rationale: Poker simulation fitness is extremely noisy (±500 BB/100 per 1,000-hand session). Same RNG seeds across all candidates within a generation make relative ranking reliable; K replicates with different seed batches per generation prevent overfitting to one seed. Static opponent field chosen over co-evolution to limit variance and complexity.

nodes.label: Betting Structure Orthogonal to Game Family
nodes.rationale: Makes no-limit/pot-limit/fixed-limit orthogonal to Holdem/Omaha/Stud/Razz so Fixed-Limit Hold'em is (Holdem, FixedLimit), not a third game; per-variant epics never fork the hand-loop machinery. The flat GameType enum is retained as the downstream compatibility surface with family()/betting() accessors layered behind it.
nodes.norm_label: betting structure orthogonal to game family

nodes.label: Data-Driven Street Descriptors
nodes.rationale: Per-family static StreetDescriptor tables (community_dealt, hole_dealt, hole_dealt_up, burn_first, bet_tier) let Stud's 5 streets and Hold'em's 4 streets share one game loop.

nodes.label: Additive Migration Strategy (smaller blast radius)
nodes.rationale: Every design-vs-actual delta in the EPIC-29 corrigendum chose the additive option: SeatHand as a new type instead of renaming HoleCards; hand field added alongside SeatNoCell.cards; ForcedBets gained a bring_in field instead of becoming an enum; Board enum migration skipped; max_raise validation deferred to variant epics with concrete callers. Goal: identical NLHE behavior with minimal churn for downstream consumers (pkpy, pknotebook, pkdealer, pkarena0-web).

nodes.label: Bring-In Selection (extreme upcard)
nodes.rationale: Lowest upcard pays bring-in for Stud Hi, highest for Razz, with suit tie-breaks. act_bring_in scans only each seat's first Up-tagged card in dealing order so the live session and hand-history replay (where all 7 cards are injected up front) pick the same bring-in seat.

nodes.label: Best-Visible-Hand Action Order
nodes.rationale: Stud action order on 4th+ streets is determined by visible hand strength, not table position (inverted for Razz). best_visible_hand_seat truncates each seat's upcard list to the count expected on the current street so live play and replay agree.

nodes.label: A-5 Lowball Evaluation
nodes.rationale: Lowest 5-of-7 wins, aces low, straights/flushes don't count, pairs are bad; nut low is the wheel 5-4-3-2-A. No inversion math was needed for the Eval bridge: HandRank::cmp is already inverted (lower value sorts higher) and CaliforniaHandRank uses lower-ordinal-is-better, so the two inversions cancel and the rank value is stored verbatim. New HandRankName::RazzLow and HandRankClass::Lowball variants tag Razz Evals.

nodes.label: Compact Hand Serialization Format (GAME_TYPE: cards - board)
nodes.norm_label: compact hand serialization format (game_type: cards - board)

nodes.label: Mental Poker (fair card game with no trusted dealer)
nodes.rationale: Separates two conflated concerns: (1) state coordination — a replicated state machine over a signed hash-linked event log, no authoritative server; and (2) card secrecy — the genuinely hard cryptography of a shuffled deck nobody can read. Concern (1) maps cleanly onto pkcore's existing deterministic fold(state, event) engine; concern (2) needs an arkworks stack pkcore deliberately avoids, which drives the crate split.
nodes.norm_label: mental poker (fair card game with no trusted dealer)

nodes.label: Barnett–Smart Deal-and-Reveal Protocol (VTMF)
nodes.rationale: Threshold ElGamal over a prime-order group: (n,n)-split aggregate key, round-robin verifiable re-mask+permute shuffle, per-card reveal tokens (partial decrypts with Chaum-Pedersen proofs) supporting reveal-to-one (hole cards) and reveal-to-all (board). Proofs at every step make it trustless rather than merely distributed.

nodes.label: CardCrypto Trait Seam
nodes.rationale: Associated types for MaskedCard and every proof keep the engine and event schema generic over the crypto scheme; the PlaintextCrypto mock (MaskedCard = Card, proofs = ()) faithfully models l-out-of-l padlock accounting so the whole game loop is testable before any curve arithmetic exists.

nodes.label: Coordinator Trait Seam (transport + ordering)
nodes.rationale: Append-and-replay over a signed hash-linked log; the only thing that differs across deployment topologies — each of the six architectures is one Coordinator impl, so topology can change without touching engine or crypto.

nodes.label: Signed Hash-Linked Event Log
nodes.rationale: prev_hash makes each event commit to the entire history (no reorder/drop/splice); seq + author legality uses the turn structure as the ordering oracle, giving ordering without consensus; equivocation is detectable because conflicting events are signed over the same prev_hash and seq. Generalizes pkcore's existing per-hand TableAction event log with a cryptographic envelope.

nodes.label: Engine Boundary Invariant (crypto never crosses into the fold)
nodes.rationale: pkcore's engine only ever sees plaintext Cards and TableActions; signatures, chain-linkage, and crypto proofs are verified at the node boundary. Swapping crypto changes the curve, swapping transport changes topology, and neither touches the engine — this keeps pkcore free of arkworks dependencies.
nodes.norm_label: engine boundary invariant (crypto never crosses into the fold)

nodes.label: pkmental Sibling Crate
nodes.rationale: Houses the Barnett-Smart card layer plus thin transport, depending on arkworks; pkcore gets only a future mental-log feature gate (Ed25519 + SHA-256 envelope). Mirrors the pkcore -> pkdealer sibling-repo pattern but with the inverted trust model: pkdealer is a trusted-server gRPC dealer, pkmental is trustless/serverless. Productionizes the throwaway pkcore-mp spike in docs/files/mentalpoker/.

nodes.label: Six Deployment Topologies (1 in-proc … 6 fully on-chain)
nodes.rationale: Recommended build path 1 -> 3 -> 5: prove crypto in-process, get a playable serverless table over a dumb relay (the literal broadcast channel Barnett-Smart assumes; one ordering point kills equivocation), then add state-channel on-chain settlement once stakes matter. #4 (semi-trusted coordinator) and #6 (fully on-chain SNARK shuffle) are branches off that spine.
nodes.norm_label: six deployment topologies (1 in-proc ... 6 fully on-chain)

nodes.label: Drop-Out Problem ((n,n) threshold stalling)
nodes.rationale: A player about to lose can stall the hand by withholding their partial decryption; needs timeout events and a forfeiture rule threading through the event log. Settlement (trustless money) and collusion (side-channel hand sharing) are separately flagged: the former is out of scope for v1, the latter unsolvable by crypto.

nodes.label: Verifiable Shuffle (Bayer–Groth argument)
nodes.rationale: Proof vs argument is a real decision-gate subtlety: a ZK proof can never be forged, an argument of knowledge is sound only against a computationally bounded adversary — the same assumption public-key crypto already rests on, so the modern reference trades it for ~50 ms prove / <1 ms verify on a 52-card shuffle.

nodes.label: QR Code Transport (experimental Coordinator)
nodes.rationale: A QR shown to the whole table is a physical broadcast channel a player cannot equivocate over. Small per-turn deltas fit one QR (~1-1.5 KB scannable); big one-time objects (masked deck ~3.3 KB, shuffle proofs) need fountain-coded animated QR (RaptorQ), as air-gapped Bitcoin wallets do. Explicitly an experimental idea, not a decision gate.

nodes.label: Card-Game Generalization (GameRules + zone/visibility algebra)
nodes.rationale: The clean factoring is not a universal Game object but a layer below: an algebra of card operations over zones (shuffle/deal/move/reveal/peek) plus a zone+visibility model, with family mid-layers (tricktaking, betting, collection). Because CardCrypto already speaks hidden/revealed-to-seat/public, pkmental generalizes to a cardgame-mp by parameterizing over the visibility model — the same move Royale makes over Kaleidoscope at the protocol level. Hard deferred parts: bidding phases, partnerships, per-game scoring, variable deck sizes, aligning the two cardpack versions (gfcore 0.7.0 vs pkcore 0.6.9).

nodes.label: Kaleidoscope: Poker Protocol with Penalty Enforcement (FC 2018)
nodes.norm_label: kaleidoscope: poker protocol with penalty enforcement (fc 2018)

nodes.label: Choose Tools for Joy, Not for The Answers
nodes.rationale: Essay against silver-bullet 'people with all the answers' (Luftschloesser); the best reason ever heard for adopting a technology was Helmut Hissen's 'you should try Java, it's a lot of fun' — things created from joy light the way. Know the imperative behind your tools and choose accordingly.
nodes.norm_label: choose tools for joy, not for the answers

nodes.label: Systems Grow by Empowering Their Domain
nodes.rationale: Contrarian stance vs Scaled Agile: scale via what we say (domain), how we say it (messaging), how we process it (business); pattern-match feedback via design-by-contract tooling.
nodes.norm_label: systems grow by empowering their domain

nodes.label: The Gold Standard (every interaction change should fail a test)
nodes.rationale: Any time you change how your code interacts with other parts of the code it should make a previously passing test fail; if a significant functional change fails no test, figure out why. Also: develop on hardware matching the deployment OS — mismatched dev machines cause the most brutal defects.
nodes.norm_label: the gold standard (every interaction change should fail a test)

nodes.label: WAMR / WASI Server-Side WASM Support
nodes.rationale: WAMR shares the .wasm format with browsers but has no JS engine, so the getrandom/uuid 'js' features produce unresolved symbols. Fix: target wasm32-wasip1, where getrandom automatically uses the WASI random_get syscall — zero source changes to game logic; only Cargo.toml target blocks split browser vs WASI. A parallel target, not a replacement for the browser WASM port.

nodes.label: Nubibus module (Pluribus log analysis)
nodes.rationale: Named Nubibus (clouds/swarm) as a pun on Pluribus. Motivation: 'I am more a data driven developer — there is no better way to drive logic than with real data'; the Pluribus struct stores parsed log state with no logic, an interim one-dimensional structure to be lifted out of Flatland into the dimensions of an actual table (button, blinds, turn order).

nodes.label: Equity vs Pot Odds Decision Gating
nodes.rationale: Without hand strength a bot with AA folds as often as one with 72o, making SimTable data engine-valid but strategically meaningless. Fast proxy: normalize HandRank into [0,1] (microseconds) instead of full RangeEquity::combined_odds (tens of ms, gated behind opt-in). Equity > 2x pot odds raises, > pot odds calls, else bluff-roll or fold; preflop uses open-raise range membership as a binary strength proxy.

nodes.label: Position-Aware Decision Routing
nodes.rationale: Position is one of the most exploitable dimensions in poker; RuleBasedDecider previously ignored Playbook position overrides and used the flat betting_strategy, so a BTN GTO profile played identically to a BB. Fix routes decisions through profile.betting_for(seat_count, position) derived from TableSnapshot.position(); falls back to flat strategy when no Playbook entry exists. dealer_button kept Option<u8> for forward compatibility with pre-game states.

nodes.label: Street-Specific Aggression Overrides
nodes.rationale: A single flat aggression_factor on every street is the most obvious tell that a bot is not playing real poker; real strategy varies preflop/flop/turn/river. StreetAggression adds optional per-street Percentage overrides resolved via aggression_for_phase(), with serde skip_serializing_if so existing YAML profiles are unchanged.

nodes.label: Type-Safe BotProfile Fields
nodes.rationale: PlayStyle as a transparent String newtype allowed YAML typos to silently produce unknown styles, and raw u8 frequency fields accepted invalid values like 150%. Replaced with a closed PlayStyle enum (8 archetypes + serde-untagged Custom(String) for backward compatibility) and a Percentage newtype validating 0..=100 at construction; custom serde keeps YAML files byte-compatible (plain integers, snake_case strings).

nodes.label: dealt_hole_cards Permanent Hole-Card Record
nodes.rationale: act_fold() mucks cards by blanking seat.cards in place, so hand-history YAMLs only had hole_cards for showdown players. A dealt_hole_cards: HashMap<u8, BoxedCards> field, populated at deal/inject time, never modified mid-hand, and cleared on reset(), preserves what was originally dealt. Typed as BoxedCards (not String) for consistency with internal card representation. Introduced in pkcore 0.0.47.

nodes.label: gRPC Dealer Service
nodes.rationale: Transforms the local dealer_repl into a network service: remote access, language-agnostic clients (Python/Go/etc.), type-safe auto-generated APIs from proto, streaming events for real-time UI updates, and easier integration testing. Dependencies are optional behind a grpc feature flag so the base library builds unchanged. Thread safety via Arc<Mutex<Dealer>>; multi-table support via session_id keyed HashMap.

nodes.label: rig_deck Deterministic-Deck Test Pattern
nodes.rationale: Random-deck smoke tests cannot assert pot distributions because cards aren't deterministic. The rig_deck helper pre-sets hole cards and replaces table.deck with a fixed sequence driving burn/flop/turn/river, enabling exact final-stack assertions. Rule: distribution semantics need engineered decks; random decks belong only in completion/panic tests.

nodes.label: Chip Conservation Is Necessary But Insufficient
nodes.rationale: Chip-conservation audits (table_chip_count == sum of starting stacks) only verify no chips were created or destroyed; chips can be conserved while routed to the wrong winner (42,445 in, 42,445 out, but split 21,222/21,223 instead of 34,985/7,460). Pot-resolution tests must assert who got the chips per seat, not just aggregate conservation.
nodes.norm_label: chip conservation is necessary but insufficient

nodes.label: Twin Implementations Are a Bug Multiplier
nodes.rationale: TableNoCell::showdown_multiway and the cell-based Showdown::process_multiway implement the same algorithm; the ==-instead-of->= bug existed line-for-line in both because they were authored as twins. Fixes and tests in one don't cover the other. Rule: when fixing a bug in TableNoCell or TableCelled, immediately check the twin file for the same code shape.
nodes.norm_label: twin implementations are a bug multiplier

nodes.label: Event-Log Shape Is a Public API
nodes.rationale: Changing which TableAction variant end_hand emits (PlayerWins vs PlayerWinsMainPot/SidePot) is a behavior change visible to every downstream event-log consumer (pkdealer, pkarena0-web, pkpy, pknotebook). The asymmetric-only delegate was chosen over always routing 2-player showdowns through multiway specifically to minimize this break. Rule: treat TableAction variant choices as part of end_hand's public contract; audit downstreams in the same PR.
nodes.norm_label: event-log shape is a public api

nodes.label: Defect A: Seat 8 Winner Not Detected
nodes.rationale: CaseEval::winning_seats() iterated 0..u8::BITS (0..8), so bit 8 (Win::NINTH, seat index 8) was never examined; a sole winner at seat 8 returned an empty vec and the entire pot was destroyed. Fix: iterate 0..self.0.len() — the runtime collection length, not a compile-time type constant. Pattern: any 0..CONST range over a collection should use collection.len().
nodes.norm_label: defect a: seat 8 winner not detected

nodes.label: Defect B: Orphaned Dead-Money Chips in Multiway Showdown
nodes.rationale: When a folded BB's contribution exceeded every active player's commitment, the only remaining TableEquity entry was Seatbit::NONE dead money; showdown_multiway's Phase 2 loop broke with no eligible seats and silently dropped the chips, caught only by the distant ChipAuditFailed check. Fix: drain remaining NONE chips to last_winner before breaking. Pattern: any loop exiting via break over a collection should assert the collection is empty on exit.
nodes.norm_label: defect b: orphaned dead-money chips in multiway showdown

nodes.label: Defect C: Seat Number vs Array Index Mismatch in Replay
nodes.rationale: HandHistory::replay() densely packed players into a Vec, violating the implicit engine-wide invariant that seat number == array index. Surfaced when a pkarena0-web session had a player leave between hands, leaving a gap seat — 'Invalid action by Seat 8: Call 0'. Fix: build a sparse array of size max(max_seat, button_seat)+1 with default empty seats filling gaps.
nodes.norm_label: defect c: seat number vs array index mismatch in replay

nodes.label: Invariant: Seat Number == Array Index
nodes.rationale: SeatsNoCell is a plain Vec<SeatNoCell> and the entire engine (apply_action, next_to_act, get_seat_mut) assumes seats[i] is physical seat i. The invariant was load-bearing but implicit — not documented, not type-enforced, not tested with sparse inputs — so the first caller reconstructing the vec from serialized data (HandHistory::replay) violated it. Prevention: state engine-correctness invariants in an # Invariants doc comment and test with non-trivial (gap-seat) inputs.

nodes.label: process_multiway Refactor: PotManager to TableEquity
nodes.rationale: The old PotManager silently skipped side pots when no overall winner was eligible (chips lost) and ignored folded players' contributions. TableEquity was already the canonical per-seat commitment representation (folded chips tracked as Seatbit::NONE, equal levels consolidated), and its winnings() method computes a winner's claimable chips and returns the leftover side pot. Key insight: chips_in_play persists across streets (only cleared by act_close_it_out), so determine_hand_equity() can be captured before close_it_out(). CaseEval is indexed by seat number because HoleCards::from(seats) iterates all seats in order.

nodes.label: Heads-Up Asymmetry Guard Dispatch Fix
nodes.rationale: Dispatching showdowns on active_in_hand().len()==2 was branching on the wrong dimension: what determines the correct payout algorithm is whether contributors committed equal amounts, not the player count. heads_up_is_symmetric() guards the fast path; asymmetric heads-up (mismatched all-ins, folded contributors) delegates to the side-pot-aware multiway path. Symmetric heads-up keeps the fast path and its PlayerWins event shape to minimize downstream breakage.

nodes.label: tied_at_level == vs >= Filter Bug
nodes.rationale: The filter e.chips == winner_chip_level excluded tied winners whose remaining commitment was higher than the layer cap. Latent for the lifetime of both showdown implementations because TableEquity::new() consolidates equal-commitment winners into one row, accidentally making == correct; only mismatched-commitment ties (a shape no existing test exercised) exposed it. Fix: == changed to >= in Phase 1 (no-cell) and Phases 1 and 2 (cell).

nodes.label: PokerSession set_blinds Deferred Blind Changes
nodes.rationale: Direct mutation of session.table.forced mid-hand rebased min_raise() against the new BB (rejecting legal raises with InsufficientIncrement) and recorded stakes that mismatched actual blind posts, breaking YAML replay. set_blinds() defers changes until the in-flight hand ends; forced_at_hand_start() snapshots the blinds at start_hand so serializers record stakes matching the actual posts. Also dropped the processed_chip_levels skip-set (distinct layers can share a numeric chip value after side-pot subtraction) in favor of a main_pot_paid toggle.

nodes.label: Short-Blind Call Target Revert (TDA Rule 41)
nodes.rationale: Reverts the 0.0.48 non-standard interpretation: when the BB posts all-in short, to_call() now returns the configured BB (standard rules, TDA Rule 41) rather than the actual posted amount; side-pot stratification and uncalled-bet returns preserve chip conservation. act_call auto-converts under-stack callers to partial all-in instead of erroring. Audit heuristic captured: never conflate 'what-actually-happened' fields (event log payload) with 'what-the-rules-require' fields (table-level call target) — each consumer of a capped 'actual' value must pull from the right source.

nodes.label: EPIC-26 Player Action Tracking and Opponent Insights
nodes.rationale: Threads a per-player Uuid through HandHistory/Action/PlayerEntry for cross-hand correlation; feature-gated analysis::player_stats aggregates VPIP/PFR/3-bet/c-bet/WTSD etc. with Confidence bands; ratios return Option<f64> to distinguish 'no data' from 0%. The from_table_state 4-tuple signature was preserved ('softening') with a new from_table_state_with_ids sibling so pkdealer and pkarena0-web compile unchanged. StatsRegistry::with_store eagerly loads (deviating from the lazy design) because interior mutability would have rippled through the Phase 3 borrow pattern.
nodes.norm_label: epic-26 player action tracking and opponent insights

nodes.label: (1+lambda) Evolution Strategy
nodes.rationale: Chosen over CMA-ES as a deliberate trade-off: full correctness with zero new crate dependencies (the cmaes crate would pull in nalgebra) over theoretical convergence speed. For n=16 bounded, moderately noisy parameters, isotropic mutation with the 1/5 rule converges comparably to CMA-ES.

nodes.label: Rechenberg 1/5 Success Rule (step-size adaptation)
nodes.author: Rechenberg (1973)
nodes.rationale: Target success probability of 1/5 derives from Rechenberg's analysis of (1+1)-ES on a sphere function: optimal progress at p_s ~ 1/(2e) ~ 18.4%. Constants c+=1.22, c-=0.90 approximately satisfy the self-consistency condition c-^4 ~ c+^-1.

nodes.label: Box-Muller Transform (Gaussian sampling)
nodes.author: Box & Muller (1958)
nodes.rationale: Basic form used (discarding Z_1) is wasteful by a factor of two but keeps code trivial; U_1 is clamped to f64::MIN_POSITIVE to avoid ln(0).

nodes.label: BB/100 fitness metric
nodes.rationale: Standard poker win-rate metric used as the stochastic objective for exploit training. Evaluator uses 1000 BB deep stacks (STARTING_CHIPS = BB * 1000) because the earlier 1B-chip design produced BB/100 values in the millions, swamping all signal; 3 replicates x 8 opponents reduce standard error ~4.9x.

nodes.label: Thin slicing (value-flow relevance program slicing)
nodes.author: Manu Sridharan, Stephen J. Fink, Rastislav Bodik
nodes.rationale: Traditional slices grow too large for human consumption because Weiser's relevance definition is overly broad; thin slices keep only copy-propagating (value-flow relevant) statements, excluding base-pointer and control dependences, reducing inspected statements up to 4.52x for debugging and 34.2x for program understanding.

nodes.label: CardCrypto trait (threshold masking scheme)
nodes.rationale: Verifiable l-out-of-l threshold masking (keygen/mask/remask/unmask) plus verifiable shuffle behind a trait so the security scheme/curve can be swapped without touching the poker engine. Engine boundary: pkcore only ever sees plaintext Card after decode; ciphertexts and proofs never enter the transition function.

nodes.label: Coordinator trait (transport + total ordering of signed event log)
nodes.rationale: Each deployment topology (in-proc, relay, mesh, state channel, chain) is one Coordinator impl, keeping deployment topology independent of crypto and engine.
nodes.norm_label: coordinator trait (transport + total ordering of signed event log)

nodes.label: Single source of truth principle
nodes.rationale: Author's experience: enterprises grind to a halt when delivery pressure cuts the single-source-of-truth corner, leaving a tangle for successors.

nodes.label: Chip conservation invariant
nodes.rationale: Total chips in play never change: every pot awarded to a winner is taken from losers (net_chips sum to zero). The showdown bugfix exists because a silent loop break orphaned dead-money chips when the BB over-contributed then folded, violating this invariant.
